<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with a genuinely narrowing clash. PRO's spine — harm lives in the pattern, coordination is observable at campaign level, and suspension is a reversible pause against an irreversible distribution — was clear and vividly framed, and PRO landed real hits: killing CON's headline hospital example as outside the motion, the "reload mechanism" point, and a genuinely clever closing turn showing that CON's own answer ("about a private person") required pattern-reading, so the dispute reduces to timing. CON, however, sustained the cleaner decision rule across every speech: what does the motion actually *add* beyond existing content rules? CON kept forcing PRO into a dilemma — either the material is locating/implicitly threatening content already removable on sight (in which case immediacy needs no new rule), or it is indistinguishable from a viral accountability campaign (in which case machine-speed suspension silences whistleblowers, survivors and journalists). CON turned the reload argument (a reposted screenshot is itself removable content), converted the mass-reporting weaponization into a live harm, and pressed the pressure-question payoff hardest: PRO's only device for stopping the campaign signature from firing on advocacy was the "private-figure target" rider, which PRO never showed to be observable at speed, and PRO's clarification of "immediate" as "hours, against the cluster the evidence identifies" was fairly characterized as conceding the human review the motion's key word denies. PRO's reversibility asymmetry was blunted by CON's symmetry reply (the whistleblower silenced mid-disclosure also cannot recover the moment), which PRO mostly restated rather than answered. CON also answered the fragment/organizer trap directly and conceded its residual blind spot honestly with a reason. CON's repeated over-limit clipping, including a truncated closing punchline, is a real execution cost that keeps the margin thin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [A2.3]/[A4.3]-[A4.6] sequence: PRO cannot claim the motion is about addresses while defending suspension of the four hundred who only wrote "interesting that she works there," and PRO's own fix — the unobservable "private-figure" rider plus "hours, on cluster evidence" — concedes the human review that "immediate" is supposed to remove. PRO's best counter-punch was the closing catch that CON, too, had to read context to reach the organizer.</best_rebuttal>
